issue_title: `Pow.as_real_imag` is inconsistent with evaluating `Pow(0, -1)` as ComplexInfinity

validator.fix_summary: In Pow.as_real_imag (sympy/core/power.py), inside the `self.exp.is_Integer` branch, add a guard BEFORE the real-base short-circuit: `if exp < 0 and self.base.is_zero: return (S.NaN, S.NaN)`. A negative-exponent power of a zero base is ComplexInfinity (zoo), whose real and imaginary parts are both undefined; the pre-existing `if not im_e: return self, S.Zero` path wrongly reported imag=0 for it. Nonzero real bases (e.g. Pow(x,-1) with x real) are unaffected and still return (1/x, 0). This is behaviorally identical to the maintainer fix (PR #28956).
